# Operators and statements

Tabular operators: 51 of 51 supported.
Descriptions are the first sentence of each entry's page in Microsoft's [KQL documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/) (CC BY 4.0); the names link there. "gokql" says whether this engine accepts the entry, probed from the code; Notes are gokql's own.

### Graph operators

| Name | gokql | Description | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| [graph-mark-components](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/graph-mark-components-operator) | yes | The `graph-mark-components` operator finds all connected components of a graph and marks each node with a component identifier. |  |
| [graph-match](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/graph-match-operator) | yes | The `graph-match` operator searches for all occurrences of a graph pattern in an input graph source. | Also reachable from GQL and openCypher (guide/graphs.md). |
| [graph-shortest-paths](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/graph-shortest-paths-operator) | yes | The `graph-shortest-paths` operator finds the shortest paths between a set of source nodes and a set of target nodes in a graph and returns a table with the results. |  |
| [graph-to-table](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/graph-to-table-operator) | yes | The `graph-to-table` operator exports nodes or edges from a graph to tables. |  |
| [make-graph](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/make-graph-operator) | yes | The `make-graph` operator builds a graph structure from tabular inputs of edges and nodes. |  |

### Tabular operators

| Name | gokql | Description | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| [as](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/as-operator) | yes | Binds a name to the operator's input tabular expression. |  |
| [consume](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/consume-operator) | yes | Consumes the tabular data stream handed to the operator. |  |
| [count](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/count-operator) | yes | Calculates the number of records in the input record set. |  |
| [datatable](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/datatable-operator) | yes | Creates a table whose schema and values are defined in the query itself. |  |
| [distinct](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/distinct-operator) | yes | Produces a table with the distinct combination of the provided columns of the input table. |  |
| [evaluate](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/evaluate-operator) | yes | Invokes a service-side query extension (plugin). | Can also start a query: evaluate http_request(...). |
| [extend](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/extend-operator) | yes | Creates calculated columns and append them to the result set. |  |
| [externaldata](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/externaldata-operator) | yes | The `externaldata` operator returns a table whose schema is defined in the query itself, and whose data is read from an external storage artifact, such as a blob in Azure Blob Storage or a file in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2. | Local paths, file:// and http(s) (callout policy); csv, tsv, psv, scsv, txt, json, multijson; .gz. |
| [facet](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/facet-operator) | yes | Returns a set of tables, one for each column specified in the facet clause. |  |
| [find](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/find-operator) | yes | Finds rows that match a predicate across a set of tables. |  |
| [fork](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/fork-operator) | yes | Runs multiple consumer operators in parallel. |  |
| [getschema](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/getschema-operator) | yes | Produce a table that represents a tabular schema of the input. |  |
| [invoke](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/invoke-operator) | yes | Invokes a lambda expression that receives the source of `invoke` as a tabular argument. |  |
| [join](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/join-operator) | yes | Merge the rows of two tables to form a new table by matching values of the specified columns from each table. |  |
| [lookup](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/lookup-operator) | yes | Extends the columns of a fact table with values looked-up in a dimension table. |  |
| [macro-expand](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/macro-expand-operator) | yes | The `macro-expand` operator simplifies running a subquery on a set of entities, such as clusters, databases, or tables, and then combining the results into a single output. | Entity groups of databases (inline or let); stored entity groups are not supported. |
| [mv-apply](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/mv-apply-operator) | yes | Applies a subquery to each record, and returns the union of the results of all subqueries. |  |
| [mv-expand](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/mv-expand-operator) | yes | Expands multi-value dynamic arrays or property bags into multiple records. |  |
| [parse](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/parse-operator) | yes | Evaluates a string expression and parses its value into one or more calculated columns. |  |
| [parse-kv](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/parse-kv-operator) | yes | Extracts structured information from a string expression and represents the information in a key/value form. |  |
| [parse-where](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/parse-where-operator) | yes | Evaluates a string expression, and parses its value into one or more calculated columns. |  |
| [partition](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/partition-operator) | yes | The partition operator partitions the records of its input table into multiple subtables according to values in a key column. | All strategies run the same way on one node. |
| [print](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/print-operator) | yes | Outputs a single row with one or more scalar expression results as columns. |  |
| [project](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/project-operator) | yes | Select the columns to include, rename or drop, and insert new computed columns. |  |
| [project-away](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/project-away-operator) | yes | Select what columns from the input table to exclude from the output table. |  |
| [project-by-names](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/project-by-names-operator) | yes | Select and reorder a subset of columns from the input table by their names, dynamic arrays, or name patterns. |  |
| [project-keep](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/project-keep-operator) | yes | Select what columns from the input to keep in the output. |  |
| [project-rename](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/project-rename-operator) | yes | Renames columns in the output table. |  |
| [project-reorder](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/project-reorder-operator) | yes | Reorders columns in the output table. |  |
| [range](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/range-operator) | yes | Generates a single-column table of values. |  |
| [reduce](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/reduce-operator) | yes | Groups a set of strings together based on value similarity. | Drain-style clustering with ADX's output shape; suited to log lines. |
| [render](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/render-operator) | yes | The `render` operator instructs the user agent to visualize query results. | Accepted; the result is returned unchanged (no charts). |
| [sample](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/sample-operator) | yes | Returns up to the specified number of random rows from the input table. |  |
| [sample-distinct](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/sample-distinct-operator) | yes | Returns a single column that contains up to the specified number of distinct values of the requested column. |  |
| [scan](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/scan-operator) | yes | Scans data, matches, and builds sequences based on the predicates. |  |
| [search](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/search-operator) | yes | Searches a text pattern in multiple tables and columns. |  |
| [serialize](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/serialize-operator) | yes | Marks that the order of the input row set is safe to use for window functions. |  |
| [sort](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/sort-operator) | yes | Sorts the rows of the input table into order by one or more columns. |  |
| [summarize](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/summarize-operator) | yes | Produces a table that aggregates the content of the input table. |  |
| [take](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/take-operator) | yes | Return up to the specified number of rows. |  |
| [top](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/top-operator) | yes | Returns the first N records sorted by the specified column. |  |
| [top-hitters](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/top-hitters-operator) | yes | Returns an approximation for the most popular distinct values, or the values with the largest sum, in the input. |  |
| [top-nested](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/top-nested-operator) | yes | The `top-nested` operator performs hierarchical aggregation and value selection. |  |
| [union](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/union-operator) | yes | Takes two or more tables and returns the rows of all of them. |  |
| [where](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/where-operator) | yes | Filters a table to the subset of rows that satisfy a predicate. |  |

## Scalar operators

37 of 37 supported. Arithmetic, comparison, logical and datetime operators are supported throughout.

## Query statements

7 of 8 supported.

### Query statements

| Name | gokql | Description | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Alias](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/alias-statement) | yes | Alias statements allow you to define an alias for a database, which can be used in the same query. | Resolves through the cluster layer (gokql.yaml). |
| [Batches](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/batches) | yes | A query can include multiple tabular expression statements, as long as they're delimited by a semicolon (`;`) character. |  |
| [Let](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/let-statement) | yes | A `let` statement is used to set a variable name equal to an expression or a function, or to create views. |  |
| [Pattern](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/pattern-statement) | yes | A pattern is a construct that maps string tuples to tabular expressions. |  |
| [Query parameters](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/query-parameters-statement) | yes | Queries sent to Kusto may include a set of name or value pairs. | The HTTP server reads properties.Parameters. |
| [Restrict](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/restrict-statement) | **no** | The restrict statement limits the set of table/view entities which are visible to query statements that follow it. | Not supported: restriction belongs to a multi-tenant service. |
| [Set](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/set-statement) | yes | The `set` statement is used to set a request property for the duration of the query. | query_now, query_bin_auto_size/at and truncationmaxrecords take effect; other options are accepted. |
| [Tabular expression statements](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/tabular-expression-statements) | yes | The tabular expression statement is what people usually have in mind when they talk about queries. |  |
